version: v115 API Error and Audit Envelope Pack
purpose: Standardize safe backend error responses, request ids, audit payloads, denial evidence, route coverage, middleware files, tests, and acceptance checks before private backend implementation starts.

denialProofScenarios.trigger: Editor requests another company record id
denialProofScenarios.expected: Return 404 not_found, write access.denied, expose no tenant hint.
Return 403 membership_admin_required and audit role/access snapshot.
Return 403 commercial_vault_denied and no value fields.
Return 401 not_authenticated with safe message and auth.login.failed audit.
Return 403 section_access_denied with route and role evidence.
Return safe replay state, no duplicate invoice or seat writes.
Return 403 section_access_denied and audit export-denied target.
Return 400 validation_error with field path and no stack trace.
Return 500 server_error with requestId only and alert event.

acceptanceChecks.note: All backend routes return ok, requestId, code, message, path, method, retryable, and safe details.
Missing and cross-tenant records share the same not_found envelope.
Every blocked section, commercial, membership, tenant, and inactive-user attempt writes evidence.
Response header, client error, server log, and audit event all share the same requestId.
Operational tracker responses and exports never include value, agreement, LOA, invoice, or negotiation fields.
Repeated billing events do not double-write invoice, subscription, seat, or audit rows.
Dry-run errors show row and field context; commit errors preserve rollback id and audit proof.
Error, audit, denial, redaction, idempotency, and route-envelope tests publish evidence files.

safeError.message: You do not have access to this restricted commercial record.

details.remediation: Ask a company admin to review access.

safeError.supportHint: Share this request id with the company admin.

handoff: v115 gives the future backend one safe response contract for every route, so UI, support, logs, audit, and CI can all trace the same request.
Frontline tracker users get operational records, while commercial and membership denials produce safe errors and audit evidence instead of accidental data leaks.
Engineering should implement request-id, typed errors, error middleware, audit context, audit writer, access denials, redaction, idempotency, and route adoption before adding deeper feature logic.
The next build can turn these tests and middleware expectations into GitHub Actions workflow files and branch-protection checks.
